svg.title: TOPAK I5 — RulesFloorNV_rev5.tla: every rules-floor entry is non-vacuous against ADR-0024 revision 5, and each property holds with its entry in force. Six invariants, each broken by dropping its entry: checked by TLC, proved by TLAPS and in Lean, and not certified
svg.desc: The module ADR-0026 §7 reports, drawn from its own text and from every results file about it, all read at build time: one havoc issuance and one promotion, the floor's entries, the six properties and the entry each rests on, every variant by every property, the witness, ADR-0026 §7's table compared row by row, every theorem and lemma, the proof run and the certified run that refused it, and the Lean re-encoding. The proofs are proved and not certified: Isabelle rejected one of Zenon's proofs, and restructuring the module is deferred by the custodian (G10 item 74). What is checked or proved here is of the module, at its constants or by its proofs, and not of the reference. The module is a frozen, dated artifact (ADR-0026 §7); the live floor is RulesFloorBase.tla (I6).

text.tspan: Proved in Lean, of the re-encoding

svg.text: Checked, proved and certified mean what ADR-0046 §1 says: TLC checks the mutations and witnesses at the module's constants; TLAPS proves each invariant under the hypothesis its statement names; the certified run accounts for every obligation by a route an independent checker accepted, or names LS4. Nothing here is said of the running reference.

Key. ① and ② are the issuance; ③ the rule set it installs; ④ the promotion, when the votes allow it. Red marks where each variant acts: an entry dropped from Active, or recusal removed. The picture is the diagram's own drawing of the definitions below.

svg.text: Satisfiability: every entry holds of Genesis.
Independence: for every entry but R9, a rule set that violates it and satisfies the others.
R9, conditionally: every rule set R9 excludes R1 excludes too, so R9's independence is stated on a floor without R1 (ADR-0026 §7 finding 1). Each is proved as a lemma (below).

svg.text: Each variant is run on the property its entry protects, and the full floor on Safe; the other cells are not run. dropR1 breaks unanimity and leaves P9_NoSoloGrant to R9; only dropR1R9 reaches a single-grant promotion (ADR-0026 §7 finding 1).

g.text: Recorded votes are counted seats, and counted seats are on the roster.
The number of recorded votes is a natural number.
P1_Unanimity is kept with R1 in force.
P2_TwoSeatsCounted is kept with R2 in force.
P5_AnchorNotApprover is kept with R5 in force.
P9_NoSoloGrant is kept with R2, and R1 or R9.
P7_BGNoAuthority is kept with R7 in force.
Base and all six, at the start.
ADR-0026 R1's property, for every behaviour, with R1 in force.
Recusal's, ADR-0024 §6, with recusal in the mechanism.
R9's, with R2 and either R1 or R9.
All six, with the whole floor and recusal.
Why norecuse must fail: the author is counted.

The run also printed: "Zenon error: could not find a proof within the memory size limit"

"A proved obligation is a theorem of the module under its assumptions and the hypotheses the statement names; the prover, not the constants, bounds the claim. Mutations and witnesses are behaviours and stay with TLC."
The proof run printed "Zenon error: could not find a proof within the memory size limit" and then "All 262 obligations proved."
The certified run's Zenon route: "ISABELLE REJECTED 1: obligations 55"; its last line: "NOT CERTIFIED: Isabelle rejected 1 of Zenon's proofs." Obligation 55 is named by number only.
Restructuring the module is deferred by the custodian (G10 item 74). Proved is not certified.
B4, the rules floor, draws the same refusal: "This proof does not certify", Isabelle rejected one of Zenon's proofs (obligation 55).
